reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with symptoms of Acute Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) Tear, often associated with meniscus injury. sharp knee pain, popping sound, and immediate swelling after twisting leg in soccer. 22F presents with acute left knee pain and rapid swelling that occurred after she planted her foot and twisted her knee during a soccer match yesterday. Recalls hearing a loud 'pop' sound and was unable to bear weight.
reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Acute Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) Tear, often associated with meniscus injury.
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Acute Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) Tear, often associated with meniscus injury.
reference_soap.plan: Assess knee alignment, effusion, ability to bear weight, and distal neurovascular status; obtain radiographs first when fracture is a concern, with MRI when examination and the clinical course support internal derangement. Provide protection, analgesia as appropriate, and early orthopedic/sports-medicine follow-up. Reconstruction is a shared decision after diagnosis and rehabilitation planning, not an automatic immediate treatment. Escalate immediately for a deformed knee, a cool/pale foot, new numbness/weakness, or pain/swelling out of proportion.

teaching.one_liner: 22F soccer player with a pop, immediate swelling, and inability to bear weight after twisting her knee.
red_flags: Immediate large effusion can indicate hemarthrosis; a deformed knee, cool/pale foot, new numbness/weakness, or pain/swelling out of proportion needs emergency assessment

must_ask.say: Can you describe how you twisted your knee and the popping sound?
How quickly did the swelling happen — right away or over hours?
Were you able to walk on it right after the injury?
How important is returning to soccer for you, and what are your concerns about surgery?

must_ask.objective: Explain the MRI and reconstruction plan
must_ask.say: After examination and any needed X-rays, an MRI may clarify a ligament injury. Treatment can include rehabilitation, and surgery is considered with a specialist based on instability, goals, and associated injuries.

history.answer: I hurt my left knee while playing soccer yesterday, heard a loud pop, and it swelled up right away.
It is just my left knee that hurts and is swollen; no other joints are affected.
It happened suddenly yesterday afternoon during a match when I planted my foot and twisted.
It was a sharp, intense pain right when it happened, about an 8 out of 10, and now it feels like a severe throbbing ache around a 6 out of 10.
My knee swelled up like a balloon within an hour or two and felt warm, but the skin is not red.
I don't have stiffness in the morning; it just feels tight and hard to bend because of all the fluid.
Trying to bend it, straighten it, or put any weight on it makes the pain much worse; keeping it still and elevated with an ice pack gives some relief.
I cannot put any weight on my left leg at all; my teammates had to carry me off the field, and I had to use crutches to get here today.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or sweating.
I planted my left foot to change direction, and my knee twisted inward. Right at that moment, I heard and felt a loud pop inside the joint.
It hasn't locked up or gotten stuck, but my knee gave out completely when I tried to put weight on it right after the injury.
No, I have never had any injury, swelling, or pain in this knee or any other joint before.
No, I have not had any fatigue, low-grade fevers, or unintended weight loss.
No, I don't have any facial rashes, scaly skin patches, mouth ulcers, hair loss, or red, irritated eyes.
No, I don't have any morning stiffness in my lower back, pain in my heels, or swollen fingers and toes.
No, I have not had any diarrhea, burning when I urinate, unusual discharge, or a recent sore throat.
I don't drink alcohol, haven't eaten unusual amounts of seafood or meat, and I don't take water pills.
I have never taken steroids or immunosuppressants, and I have never had injections or surgery in any joint.
I am not currently sexually active, and I do not have a new sexual partner.
I am terrified that I tore my ACL or knee ligaments and that I won't be able to play soccer again.
I am really anxious about whether I will need surgery to fix my knee.
I was hoping to get an MRI to see what is torn and get a supportive knee brace.
I don't have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes, high blood pressure, or arthritis.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I am not taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter pain relievers, or herbal supplements.
I don't have any allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes or used vape products.
I don't drink alcohol at all.
I am a 22-year-old college student and play competitive soccer on the university team, living in a campus dormitory.
No one in my family has rheumatoid arthritis, gout, or any other autoimmune or joint conditions.
My last period started about two weeks ago, my menstrual cycles are regular every 28 days, and there is no possibility of pregnancy.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, pulse 76 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, body temperature 36.7°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.

Tense effusion and moderate warmth of the left knee with positive patellar tap; joint line tenderness and positive Lachman test; range of motion is restricted by pain and swelling; right knee is normal.
Antalgic gait with inability to bear weight on the left leg; patient requires crutches to ambulate.
Bilateral dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses are 2+ and symmetric; feet are warm with capillary refill under 2 seconds.
Light touch sensation is intact across bilateral lower extremities, including the web space between the first and second toes and the plantar surface.
No skin rash, psoriasis plaques, malar erythema, tophi, or petechiae observed on any extremities or face.
